conviction_note: The findings are small and mixed and add to +0.3. Two independent Q3 series point to a modest beat on the 1,195 MEUR comparable-EBITDA bar: TotalEnergies' European refining marker was 33.2 $/bbl (13.5 in Q2), and Enilive's EBIT rose from 0.295 bn to 0.41 bn quarter on quarter. Against that sit Diamond Green Diesel's margin per gallon falling 36% QoQ and a real risk that the renewables volume guide gets trimmed. So print_vs_bar is +4 but p_up only 54: the stock sold its record Q2 (-6.4%) and has already fallen about 18% from its 24 Sept high on October crack weakness. abs_move is 8 because the numbers are new and this name's confirmed print reactions run 6-13%. The scaled +0.64 and the +0.3 sum agree in sign and differ only because they are separate measurements.

Q2 working capital build of EUR 842m, mainly inventory built ahead of the planned refinery maintenance, so a Q3 release is flagged

new_in_release.expect: Comparable EBITDA modestly above the 1,195 MEUR Vara consensus. Oil Products refining margin above the ~36 $/bbl analyst assumption; RP sales margin flat-to-up versus the ~1,150 $/t estimate.
RP volume guide ('approximately same level as 2025') reiterated more likely than not. A trim to 'slightly lower' is a real tail, given H1 at 1,900 kt and two RP turnarounds in Q4.
Strong Q3 cash flow before financing as the Q2 inventory build unwinds; leverage down from 29.9%. Positive.
Q4 market commentary probably cautious: October gasoil cracks falling, HVO-diesel spread compressing, Rotterdam and Singapore turnarounds. Already partly in the -18% drawdown.

findings.finding: TotalEnergies' European Refining Margin Marker averaged 33.2 $/bbl in Q3 2026 against 13.5 in Q2. Neste's total refining margin has run 5-12 $/bbl above that marker (Q2'25 10.0 vs 4.7; Q2'26 25.8 vs 13.5), which implies roughly 39-45 $/bbl for Q3 against the ~36 $/bbl in the Inderes and consensus numbers. The Porvoo turnaround caps the refined barrels this applies to.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 record Oil Products (25.8 $/bbl) within a record quarter: stock -6.4% on 2026-07-24. Q1'26 beat: +6.3% on 2026-04-29.
findings.why_not_priced: Inderes raised to 36 $/bbl on 21 Oct, after the TotalEnergies indicator, and still sits below the marker-plus-historical-premium range. The Vara consensus (1,195) is no higher than Inderes, and its 803 low shows stale estimates inside it. If this were priced, the stock would not have fallen 10% over the 20 days the indicator has been public.
findings.independence: US 3-2-1 crack averaged 64.5/65.6/68.2 $/bbl in Jul/Aug/Sep versus 53.2/47.8 in May/Jun (EIA-based): https://globaloilshock.com/en/data/crack-spread-chart/. Q2 TotalEnergies ERM 13.5 per its official table: https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260715079580/en/TotalEnergies-SE-Second-Quarter-2026-Main-Indicators

findings.finding: Eni's Enilive, Neste's main European HVO/SAF peer, reported Q3 2026 proforma adjusted EBIT of EUR 0.41bn (Q2: EUR 295m, +39% QoQ), 'driven by the biorefining business, which benefited from an improved market scenario'. The consensus has Neste's RP sales margin down about 6% QoQ (1,150 vs 1,223 $/t).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RP margin is the line this name trades on. The record 1,223 $/t in Q2 was sold (-6.4%); the RP margin upside in Q1'26 and Q1/Q2'25 printed +6.3%, +12.0% and +12.8%.
findings.original_quote: Q2 base, Eni Q2 release (Italian): 'Nel secondo trimestre 2026, il business Enilive ha registrato un utile operativo proforma adjusted di €295 mln' = 'In Q2 2026 Enilive posted proforma adjusted operating profit of EUR 295m'
findings.why_not_priced: Eni reported on 23 Oct, after the Inderes preview (21 Oct) and the Vara consensus snapshot (consensus target raised to 37 on 20 Oct), so the bar predates it. Neste has fallen since. Part of Enilive's QoQ gain is seasonal marketing, so the read-through is partial.

findings.finding: Diamond Green Diesel's (Valero) renewable diesel margin fell from $2.52/gal in Q2 to $1.62/gal in Q3 2026 (-36%). Management blamed mostly DGD-specific items (Q2 one-offs, a storm, lower PTC capture on foreign feedstock) but also feedstock price lag and a D4 RIN drop, both of which touch Neste's 27% North America volumes.
findings.why_not_priced: Valero's segment detail is a US read that Nordic coverage rarely models line by line. It may partly explain the late-October weakness, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Q2 base $2.52/gal from Valero's Q2 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1035002/000162828026050822/a6302026exh9901earningsrel.htm. Management's causes are in the call: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/22/valero-vlo-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

findings.finding: Neste's own H1 table puts RP sales at 1,900 kt against 4,134 kt for 2025. Holding the 'approximately same level' guide needs roughly 2.0-2.2 Mt in H2, above the record-pace Q2 (1,026 kt), while Rotterdam (8 wks, Q4) and Singapore (11 wks from Dec) are down. Utilisation was 71% in H1, so a trim of the volume guide is a real tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2025 (Q4'24 with a weak RP outlook): -10.5% on 2025-02-13. A volume-guide cut historically moves this name high single digits.
findings.why_not_priced: Inderes expects the guide to be reiterated ('full-year production outlook unchanged'), and the consensus margin focus ignores the volume arithmetic. Probability-weighted (about 25-30% chance of a trim) because trading volumes now count toward sales and inventory can bridge the gap.
findings.independence: Inderes flagged in July that RP production was 14% behind the comparison period at end-H1: https://www.inderes.fi/files/9fd83a8d-ab10-495a-bb85-c20a087dd514. A forum poster (post 4106, 2026-10-28) names weak production volumes as 'Nesteen ainut riski': https://forum.inderes.com/t/neste-ilmastonmuutostaistelun-eturivissa/252

findings.why_not_priced: Previews (Inderes) focus on EBITDA and margins and print no cash-flow line. An inference from the company's own statement, so it is sized small.

Against that, HVO rebounded about $300/t and UCO feedstock fell about $50/t by 27 Oct. The release's market commentary is likely cautious on Q4.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive (+0.3) and agree with the small run-up lean (+0.51, mean reversion after -10.3% over 20d). They cut against the tape's recent direction, which the October crack and HVO-spread weakness explains, and the name's habit of selling records pulls p_up toward 50.
